title: Know What a Cash-Flowing Asset Really Is
hook: An asset is not valuable because somebody called it passive.
outcome: A repeatable method to evaluate ownership, cash flow, durability, and risk.
steps: Identify the legal or practical ownership right and what control it actually gives you.
Map gross inflows, operating costs, taxes, maintenance, financing, vacancies, refunds, and labor.
Calculate net cash flow under normal, downside, and break-even assumptions.
Assess concentration, liquidity, legal, technical, market, and operator dependency risks.
Define what evidence would prove the asset is improving or deteriorating.
cta: Save this before buying an 'income asset.'
disclaimer: Educational only, not investment, tax, or legal advice. Verify assumptions with qualified professionals.

title: Build a Digital Product That Gets Better After Every Sale
hook: A file becomes an asset when delivery, support, measurement, and improvement are systemized.
outcome: A sellable digital product with automated delivery and a learning loop.
steps: Choose one narrow outcome already requested by a real audience.
Create the smallest complete product: instructions, templates, examples, validation, and support boundaries.
Connect checkout, tax settings, receipts, delivery, access control, refunds, and analytics.
Capture activation, completion, support friction, refund reason, and customer outcome.
Update the product from evidence and version every release.
cta: Comment PRODUCT for the asset checklist.
disclaimer: Follow payment, tax, consumer-protection, privacy, and platform requirements that apply to your location and customers.

title: Protect the Work Your Business Creates
hook: Ownership becomes expensive to untangle after money and collaborators arrive.
outcome: A basic intellectual-property and access-control inventory.
steps: List brand names, domains, code, designs, content, customer data, processes, and inventions.
Record who created each item, under what agreement, and where the source files live.
Use written contractor and employee agreements appropriate to your jurisdiction.
Control repository, domain, cloud, payment, and social account access through business-owned accounts.
Track registrations, licenses, renewals, third-party components, and evidence of creation.
cta: Share this with every founder using personal accounts for company assets.
disclaimer: This is general education, not legal advice. Intellectual-property rules and contract requirements vary.

title: Score a Small Business Before You Buy It
hook: Revenue can be real while the business is still unbuyable.
outcome: A first-pass acquisition scorecard that exposes dependencies and verification needs.
steps: Verify revenue using bank, processor, tax, invoice, and customer evidence—not a spreadsheet alone.
Normalize owner pay, one-time expenses, deferred maintenance, refunds, debt, and required working capital.
Measure customer, supplier, employee, channel, location, and owner concentration.
Inspect contracts, licenses, litigation, security, privacy, assets, liabilities, and transferability.
Build downside scenarios and a diligence list before discussing valuation or financing.
cta: Comment ACQUIRE for the diligence scorecard.
disclaimer: Business acquisitions require legal, accounting, tax, operational, and often industry-specific professional review.
